title: Cascade Batch Sherpa: workload-aware batching advisor with staged safe-apply
creator: Amelia Ruiz
description: Goal: Build a continuous, workload-driven batching recommendation engine (a.k.a. 'Cascade Batch Sherpa') that profiles live traffic, suggests conservative batching & cache configs, and performs staged safe-apply with automated rollback triggers. Scope: profiling pipeline, heuristic selector, continuous parameter adaptation loop, canary/shadow apply orchestration, telemetry & alerting. Out of scope for this ticket: UI surface in Console (will be separate PM ticket), full RBAC controls for enterprise private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Production profiling pipeline emits daily workload fingerprints for each route, 2) Heuristic model produces candidate batch_size / batching_window / prefix_cache settings with estimated cost delta and latency impact, 3) Safe-apply orchestrator can perform shadow apply, 1% canary, and auto-rollback if any telemetry threshold is breached, 4) Integration tests and a dry-run mode exist and show no change to live traffic before canary, 5) Documentation and runtime-1.26 release notes include behavioral description and telemetry queries.
implementation_notes: Design: 1) Workload profiler aggregates per-route metrics (seq_len distribution, arrival inter-arrival time, token-per-request, KV-hit ratio) into a compact fingerprint (stable hash + histograms). 2) Heuristic scoring engine maps fingerprints to a Pareto front of candidate configs using conservative cost/latency trade-off rules derived from offline microbenchmarks. 3) Continuous tuner runs a low-frequency hill-climb (or Bayesian bandit with safety margin) to propose parameter deltas that are shadow-tested before canary. 4) Safe-apply orchestration: shadow apply -> observe internal metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, OOMs, error rate) -> canary rollout 1% -> ramp with backoff up to configured cap. Trade-offs: prioritize latency SLOs over cost savings; prefer smaller batch increases on latency-sensitive routes; maintain explicit per-customer isolation flags for Dedicated/Private. Implementation will reuse existing profiler infra (ENG-7421) and batching microbench data (ENG-33120).
telemetry_queries: cost_delta_query: SELECT sum(tokens)*unit_cost FROM token_usage WHERE route=$route AND after_config=true - before_config=true
latency_p99: SELECT percentile_cont(0.99) FROM latency_ms WHERE route=$route AND window=5m
error_rate: SELECT count(status>=500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE route=$route AND window=5m
kv_hit_rate: SELECT sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups) FROM kv_metrics WHERE route=$route AND window=1h
telemetry_thresholds: latency_p99_increase_threshold: 10% relative increase over baseline -> rollback
oom_or_mem_eviction: any occurrence during canary -> immediate rollback
cost_increase_threshold: N/A (we only apply cost-reducing suggested configs)
rollout_plan: 1) Nightly profiler runs; generate candidate list and confidence scores, 2) Run shadow apply on staging cluster for the top candidate for 24h, 3) Start canary at 1% traffic for 30m; monitor 5m windows, automated checks every 1m, 4) If stable, ramp to 5% for 1h, then 25% for 2h with manual gate, 5) Full apply only after 24h stable at >=25% and cost regressions validated in metrics, 6) Post-apply monitoring for 72h with digest report to #cost-ops channel.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback if any rollback trigger fires (telemetry thresholds above) during shadow or canary. Manual rollback procedure: 1) Open incident in PagerDuty with 'Cascade Batch Sherpa' runbook, 2) Revert to previous config via rollout controller (single flag flip), 3) Run postmortem with timeline and root cause including profiler artifacts, 4) Re-run candidate selection with tightened safety margins and block same candidate until manual review.
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and scoring; integration tests that simulate synthetic workloads (high burst, long-tail seq_len, KV-heavy) and assert no P99 regression > baseline threshold when applying conservative candidate; e2e dry-run that runs on shadow mode against the prod read-replica cluster; load tests in perf lab with representative models and quantization settings.
